ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A hidden sodium load

A 70-year-old man with heart failure follows a sodium-restricted diet. He begins taking sodium bicarbonate several times daily for recurrent heartburn. Over the following week his weight and ankle edema increase. Which property of this remedy is most relevant to the worsening congestion?

  1. Inhibition of intestinal sodium absorption
  2. Chelation of serum calcium into insoluble salts
  3. Selective stimulation of cardiac beta1 receptors
  4. Delivery of an absorbable sodium load
  5. Direct blockade of renal mineralocorticoid receptors
Answer and explanation

Delivery of an absorbable sodium load

Sodium bicarbonate adds sodium and can worsen fluid retention in susceptible patients.

Option explanations

Delivery of an absorbable sodium load: Absorbed sodium can aggravate edema and congestion.

Direct blockade of renal mineralocorticoid receptors: Mineralocorticoid blockade tends to promote sodium loss.

Inhibition of intestinal sodium absorption: Blocking sodium absorption would not explain a positive sodium balance.

Chelation of serum calcium into insoluble salts: Calcium chelation is not the mechanism of sodium-related congestion.

Selective stimulation of cardiac beta1 receptors: Sodium bicarbonate is not a selective cardiac adrenergic agonist.
